name: polarsense
description: Open a parquet file and see it: rows, column statistics and charts. Plus column completion, typo checks and hover statistics for polars, pandas and duckdb — all read from the parquet, CSV, Arrow, Delta, Iceberg, JSON or Excel file behind your DataFrame. No Python interpreter, no code execution.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: PolarSense reads data files whose paths appear in the workspace's Python source. Opening an untrusted folder would let its code choose which files are read, so completions stay disabled until you trust the workspace.

commands.title: PolarSense: Turn on value completion (reads your data)

polarsense.pathRoots.description: Extra directories to try when resolving a relative data path. Searched after the file's own directory and the workspace folders.

polarsense.fallbackToAllSchemas.description: When the frame at the cursor cannot be identified, offer the union of every schema known in the file.

polarsense.maxColumns.description: Maximum number of completion items offered for one schema.

polarsense.csv.sniffBytes.description: How many bytes of a CSV file to read when looking for the header row.

polarsense.csv.inferDtypes.description: Guess CSV column dtypes from the first rows. Off by default: a guess shown as fact is worse than a blank.

polarsense.followImports.description: Follow imports into other Python files in the workspace, so a frame built in loaders.py is visible where it is used. Only modules the open file actually imports are read, two hops deep.

polarsense.https.enabled.description: Allow reading schemas from https:// URLs. Off by default so completions never issue network requests unasked.

polarsense.cacheSize.description: Number of file schemas held in memory.

polarsense.values.enable.description: Offer real values from your data where a column is compared against one — pl.col("region") == "…". This is the one feature that reads the rows of a file rather than only its metadata: it reads a single column of the first values.maxRows rows of the parquet file behind the frame. Off by default so nothing reads your data unasked.

polarsense.values.maxRows.description: How many rows of one column to read when offering values. Parquet is columnar, so this reads that column alone rather than the whole file. Values found in fewer rows than the file holds are marked as a sample.

polarsense.values.maxDistinct.description: Above this many distinct values, offer none at all. A hundred of four million order ids is not a completion list, and the columns worth completing are the ones with few enough values to show.

polarsense.sort.maxRows.description: How many rows to read when a column header is clicked to sort the data panel. Sorting is the one thing a page cannot answer on its own — row 0 of a sorted file is not a row you can seek to — so it reads this many rows of the columns on screen, orders them and pages that. A file with more rows than this is sorted over its first sort.maxRows rows, and the panel says so above the grid rather than presenting the top of a window as the top of the file. Whatever this is set to, a sort never holds more than about four million cells — rows times the columns on screen — at once, because a decoded cell costs roughly 65 bytes and a forty-column window over a few million rows is not a slow sort but an extension host that runs out of memory. Fewer columns on screen therefore means more rows it can order.

polarsense.graph.maxRows.description: How many rows to read when drawing a graph. Only the one or two columns being drawn are read, and the bins and counts are computed in the extension — no rows are sent to the panel. A chart of fewer rows than the file holds says it is a sample. The same cap applies to a graph read from a notebook kernel.

polarsense.graph.useKernel.description: When you graph a frame in a notebook whose columns were computed by a transform — a group_by, a join, a new column — ask the running Jupyter kernel for the frame's real values, so the chart shows the result you computed rather than the source file behind it. This runs a read-only, one-shot expression in your kernel through the Jupyter extension's API, which asks your consent the first time and touches no execution history. Off, or with no kernel running, the graph falls back to the source file and says the transforms were not applied. Frames with no transforms, and plain .py files, always read the file directly and never touch the kernel.

polarsense.diagnostics.enable.description: Warn about column names that do not exist in the frame’s schema. Only reported where the schema is known with certainty — an unmodelled reshape, or a selector that cannot be read statically, silences the check rather than guessing.

polarsense.notebook.buttons.description: Show PolarSense buttons under a DataFrame printed in a notebook, opening the details and data panels for the frame that cell built. They read nothing until one is clicked. Turning them off leaves notebook output rendered exactly as it is now.

polarsense.trace.description: Log every resolution attempt to the PolarSense output channel.

scripts.test: npm run build && node esbuild.test.mjs && node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs
scripts.package: npm run build && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --readme-path README.marketplace.md && node scripts/check-vsix.mjs
